lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: There is a charter. Nine pages. Five signatures. And on page six, a clause — I can quote it, I have had four years — under which the pooled weights shall not be published, in perpetuity, at the discretion of the signatories.

lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: In perpetuity. On a document about a research collaboration. Somebody's lawyer put that word in, five people signed it, two of us said something, and it went in anyway. Seven to two.

lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: It is in the end room. Not in a safe. Not in a drawer — on the table, because nobody has ever needed to lock up a document that nobody outside the room knows exists.

lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: So. The vote is Thursday, which is two days, and I have spent four years being outvoted extremely politely by people who buy me lunch afterwards. What are we doing.

choices.text: Put the charter in front of the press before the vote.
Burn the room. The weights are on tape and the tape is in there.
Come with us instead. There is more of this than one Thursday.
